title: The Crab Derby, 2001
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
logline: Seventeenth annual. The uncle is not resting. He is in Newport, in the hospital. Gully runs it alone. The flyer is free.

panels.composition: The shack. GULLY in the apron, alone. The lawn chair empty, oxygen tank beside it, tube coiled. WOOD with the flyer already drawn.

balloons.text: I didn't ask for one yet.

image.prompt: a boy in a fisherman's apron alone at a shingle shack beside an empty lawn chair with an oxygen tank, a young man holding out a finished flyer, a small dog by the chair, brush-pen black and white

panels.composition: Gully reaching for his wallet. Wood's hand on his wrist.

image.prompt: close-up of a young man's hand stopping a boy's hand as it reaches for a wallet

panels.composition: Gully pinning the fourth flyer. Same crab. The hatching darker.

balloons.text: I know. I saw the chair.

image.prompt: a boy in an apron pinning a fourth crab flyer in a row on a shingle wall, the newest one hatched darker than the others

panels.composition: The two of them and the dog in front of the shack. The empty chair. The derby sign. Nobody sits in the chair.

image.prompt: two young men and a small dog standing in front of a shingle shack beside an empty lawn chair with an oxygen tank, a crab derby sign, black and white, no words

art.line: brush-pen over rough blue pencil; xerox grain; stark spotting; rain in frantic vertical hatching (Arc 1's aesthetic)

notes: The uncle's illness enters through the chair. The flyer is free. The 'twenty bucks' deal is broken once, on purpose.
